items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that two tautologically equivalent families with a fixed target give the same sheaf condition for every presheaf (statement lines 1398-1410). The proof is a complete argument in one direction, the other being symmetric: a compatible family for one family is transported along the isomorphisms provided by the tautological equivalence to a compatible family for the other (proof lines 1413-1434), the sheaf condition for the latter produces a unique amalgamation, and the author verifies by producing an isomorphism onto a fibre product that the amalgamation restricts to the original sections (proof lines 1435-1442). The non-formal content is the transport of the compatibility conditions along the isomorphisms. The claim is H2: a written-out implication with the symmetry noted.
